title: Why he never learned to arrange
summary: Roy had no eyes for arranging, writing only intros and a few bars, and reflects on being too busy playing.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I know a lot of the people in that band arranged. Did you do any arranging at that time?
No, I never had any eyes for that. No. Only time I almost got into that was when I was in the Arcadia,

you know. I wrote an introduction on something. The band sounded so good, and I used to get high and borrow this paper, and go and get high... And I got more four-bars or eight-bars written down than anybody in the world! But that's as far as I could get, you know. Heh-heh.

No, I was busy tootin'... You see, with me, I was too busy trying to play. You know, and I'd prepare myself for the things I would eventually get to, and I did... But then what I got to was such a farce, man, you know...! I mean, you think you go through life trying to get yourself straight, and you reach a goal, and there's still a fence out there. See, that's what hurts. See, I think that's what just turned me off completely, or else I would have been able to play better than I was playing, you know.
